## Refinement — the tracker is not always worktree-LOCAL, and the symlink case is worse

A second agent checked its own exposure while closing `wolflike-chevroned-haddock` and found a
different topology in its worktree: `.tickets-tracker` was a **symlink to the shared
`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker`**, not a worktree-local copy.

That is not a reassuring variant. It **widens** the hazard rather than narrowing it, because the
two topologies fail in opposite directions from the same trigger — running a check from inside a
worktree:

| topology | what `git -C .tickets-tracker …` actually touches | failure mode |
|---|---|---|
| worktree-LOCAL copy | that worktree's private tracker | **retirement destroys unpushed events** (the original finding) |
| **symlink to shared** | the SHARED tracker | **a check believed to be scoped to this worktree silently operates on shared state** |

So a session cannot reason about the risk from "am I in a worktree?" alone. It has to know which
topology it has, and **nothing in the workflow prompts that question**.

The symlink case makes the cwd-drift failure this ticket already documents materially more
dangerous. The original observation was that a bare `HEAD` check was correct only by luck
because the shell's cwd had drifted into the tracker worktree. Under the symlink topology the
same drift does not merely produce a lucky-correct answer — it produces an answer about the
**shared** tracker while the operator believes it is about this worktree's. A verification that
reports "0 unpushed" can be describing a different store than the one being retired.

Both agents independently converged on the same defence, which is worth recording as the
practice regardless of which remedy this ticket lands: **use `git -C <absolute path>` with
explicit `refs/heads/tickets` and `refs/remotes/origin/tickets`, never a bare `HEAD`**, and
confirm event CONTENT on the origin-tracked tree rather than inferring it from ref equality.
The second agent verified `COMPLETION_VERDICT`, `STATUS`, `SIGNATURE` (including that
`head_sha` matched the merged commit) and the `caused_by` LINK by reading them, not by comparing
SHAs alone.

Note this also affects the remedy options already listed. A pre-retirement guard that inspects
`<worktree>/.tickets-tracker` would, under the symlink topology, inspect the shared tracker and
report healthy — correctly, and uselessly, since nothing worktree-local was at risk. Whatever
is chosen has to resolve the symlink and state which store it is talking about.
